clue.text: Make merry, ultimately wonderful musical

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the following word, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: to carouse is to drink and make merry noisily
the final letter of wonderful

explanation.surface: A cheerful instruction to celebrate, finishing with praise for a wonderful stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Carousel is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, an example of the broader category named.

clue.text: A bit pale, lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking says the word that follows is missing something, so a letter is dropped from it

blocks.note: pale and white are both words for a colourless complexion
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone looks slightly washed out, as if drained of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit pale' reads as one phrase, but 'A bit' is the definition and pale is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is a tiny amount, as in 'not a whit', so it matches a small quantity.

clue.text: God willing, old king shall receive artist and composer

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: DV abbreviates the Latin Deo volente, meaning God willing
O is a standard abbreviation for old
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A pious promise that an elderly monarch will welcome a painter and a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: DV for 'God willing' is the Latin Deo volente, often written at the end of old letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak was the Czech nineteenth-century writer of the New World Symphony, so he is a classical music maker.

clue.text: Oh, can't I be put to work in the old city?

indicators.note: letters put to work are set to a new task and moved about into a different order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Someone protests at being made to labour in an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch was an important ancient city of Syria, now Antakya in Turkey, so it is an historic town.

clue.text: Idiot Russian dog endlessly runs away

indicators.note: endlessly says the word loses its tail, so its final letter is cut
something sent away is taken out, so this letter leaves the word

blocks.note: the borzoi is a Russian wolfhound
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A foolish hound from Russia keeps running off without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut the last letter of BORZOI, then remove its R, to leave BOZO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bozo is American slang for a stupid or clownish person, a fool.

clue.text: Greek humour failure following loss of a uniform guerrilla army

indicators.note: loss of says a letter goes missing from the phrase before it
a failure is a breakdown, so these letters collapse and re-form in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A joke from Athens falls flat after a uniform goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: One U goes from GREEK HUMOUR, and the ten letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Khmer Rouge were the Cambodian communist insurgents who fought a jungle war before seizing power in 1975.

clue.text: An early Christian from France, I sat above the Catholic church

indicators.note: in a down entry one part sitting above another means it comes first in the answer

blocks.note: je is French for I
Rome stands for the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: A French believer describes his seat high above a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Jerome, translator of the Vulgate Bible, was a fourth-century father of the Church, a figure from its first centuries.

clue.text: Where the rich hope to avoid the call of duty?

definitions.text: Where the rich hope to avoid the call of duty?

blocks.clueFragment: Where the rich hope to avoid the call of duty?
blocks.note: surface reading: a place where privileged people dodge military service
setter's reading: duty is a levy on money, and the call is the demand to pay it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Call of duty' suggests being summoned to serve; here duty means a charge owed to the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealthy people move money to low-levy countries precisely to escape paying what governments charge them.

clue.text: Task shifting to the front ordinary mineral earth

indicators.note: shifting to the front means one letter is lifted out and placed at the start instead

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
a chore is a routine task

explanation.surface: A job moves forward, involving some everyday soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The O in CHORE moves from the middle to the start, giving OCHRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a natural clay pigment, iron oxide in soil, used for yellow and brown paints.

clue.text: Oscar punches belly - it's extremely painful

indicators.note: a fist that punches goes into the body, so one piece is driven inside another

blocks.note: the gut is the belly
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar thumps someone in the stomach, and it really hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gout is an inflammatory joint disease, notorious for agonising swelling of the big toe.

clue.text: 9-iron's used in big game

indicators.note: used letters are worked over and handled, ending up in a new arrangement

blocks.note: the answer to 9 across
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A golfer reaches for a 9-iron in an important match.
explanation.walkthrough: '9-iron' looks like a golf club; the 9 is a cross-reference to another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Big game means large wild animals hunted for sport, and the rhinoceros is one of the classic examples.

clue.text: It is OK - it is OK - periodically to express disapproval thus

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter of the text is taken

blocks.clueFragment: It is OK - it is OK
blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Someone repeatedly reassures, though the words come with a disapproving tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled click of the tongue is the sound people make to show they disapprove, written as an interjection.

clue.text: Instrument Mike installed in boat adrift on water

indicators.note: a boat adrift drifts loosely, so its letters float into a new order
something installed in a place is fitted inside it
in a down entry one piece sitting on another comes before it

blocks.note: taken as written
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to pass water is to urinate, so water stands for urine

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is placed in a drifting boat out on the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' as urine is a crossword favourite, from 'passing water'; in a down entry 'on' puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a small hand drum with jingling metal discs, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: "Internet relations beginning to corrupt Yankee bishop" - Gaelic Times

indicators.note: beginning to points to the start of the next word, so only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of corrupt
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a churchman led astray by online affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks and 'Gaelic Times' make it look like a tabloid headline from an Irish paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Cybersex is sexual interaction conducted online, so it amounts to intimate dealings over the web.

clue.text: British/American coach

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a large passenger road vehicle, much the same as the everyday public transport vehicle.

clue.text: Like a chap from Brussels getting himself confused?

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up and come out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Belgian man becomes muddled, perhaps over the country's languages.
explanation.definitionFit: Flemish describes the Dutch-speaking people of Flanders, and Brussels has many such residents.

clue.text: Step over 25?

indicators.note: in a down entry a word turned over is flipped and read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pas is a step in ballet

explanation.walkthrough: 25 refers to the answer at 25 down, CLOT, meaning a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap is a gullible, foolish person, so it is a synonym for a dimwit or idiot.

clue.text: An insignificant person Henry, the former Prime Minister

blocks.note: taken as the single letter
squit is British slang for a small, contemptible person
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about a nobody named Henry who once led the government.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a first name (Asquith's was Herbert Henry), but it is the scientific unit.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was the Liberal leader of the British government from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Initially take steps to cover each social gathering

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the word, so only its first letter is used
to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the first letter of take
a dance is a series of steps
ea is the standard abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: Advice to make a start on organising a party for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies only to the word take; steps is a whole word, and the two together wrap around the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea dance is an afternoon party with refreshments and ballroom dancing, a kind of social occasion.

clue.text: Very dry area within North-Eastern Crete was her home

indicators.note: within says one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: arid means extremely dry
A is the abbreviation for area
NE abbreviates north-east

explanation.surface: A description of a parched region in the north-east of a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ariadne was the daughter of King Minos of Crete who helped Theseus escape the Minotaur's labyrinth.

clue.text: Paragraph writer Saul half-heartedly starts, being a bit ill

indicators.note: half-heartedly says part of the heart, the middle of the name, is lost
starts means this piece comes at the beginning, before the other

blocks.note: Saul Bellow was the American author of Herzog
par is a common abbreviation for paragraph

explanation.surface: A nervous author named Saul hesitantly begins a new paragraph while feeling under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul Bellow was a Nobel-winning American novelist; losing half the heart means one of the two central letters goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below par means not quite well, the idiom drawn from golf's standard score.

clue.text: Former partner, a tango specialist

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
per means a, as in twice per day
T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone's ex-partner is a skilled tango dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' means 'each', so it gives PER, as in 'ten pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a person with special skill or knowledge, the same as a specialist.

clue.text: Local rule using benchmark interest rate as specified by Spooner

indicators.note: William Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starting sounds trade places

blocks.note: LIBOR was the London interbank lending rate used as a benchmark

explanation.surface: A town council's regulation is tied to a key banking rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Say LIBOR as 'lie-bor' and swap the opening sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A byelaw is a regulation made by a council or local authority rather than national government.

clue.text: Large bloke from ABBA's catching fish

indicators.note: catching means taking hold of something and holding it inside

blocks.note: Benny Andersson was one of the two men in ABBA
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big man from the Swedish pop group goes fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The blenny is a small spiny-finned fish of rocky shores and rock pools.

clue.text: Treasure to rise in value

blocks.note: first meaning: to value highly and be grateful for
second meaning: to grow in worth, as property does

explanation.walkthrough: Treasure looks like a noun for hidden gold; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both cherishing something dearly and an asset becoming worth more over time.

clue.text: Wally, bed-ridden student

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A fool of a student who never gets out of bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Wally is British slang for a silly person, not a name here.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British insults for a stupid, clumsy person.

clue.text: Boyfriend, upper-class Republican kicked out of office

blocks.note: a bureau is an office or agency
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.walkthrough: BUREAU loses one U and its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male suitor or sweetheart.

clue.text: Spa putting up hotel bill

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: A health resort raises the cost of a night's stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is the English city famous for its Roman hot springs, the original British spa town.

blocks.note: the inner letters of crone
a do is a party

explanation.walkthrough: 'Party piece' reads as one phrase, but piece alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical work whose main theme keeps returning, so it is a piece of music.

clue.text: Pen a note chiding parcels biz delivering small items

blocks.note: letters running across these words
